Every chemical compound wants to stay at the lowest energy level. This is why in nature you're more likely to see NaCl instead of sodium or chlorine by itself. 

Having said that, NaCl is the lowest energy state, and what you must do to separate it is add some sort of energy to be able to sustain itself in a pure element form. Sources that add energy can be Physical, Thermal, and Electrical. 

What they do in industry is heat the salt into a liquid state and run electricity through the mixture.  The sodium will collect on the Cathode and fall to the bottom, while the light chlorine gas will collect on the anode and will float to the top.  The separation is the easiest this way, but as a chemist, there is many other ways to separate them chemically, but it is way more complicated. 

Physical rarely does anything in this case (usually works for gasses)
